title: Let the Whole Race of Creatures Lie
description: Let the Whole Race of Creatures Lie in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 145 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Decrees and Providence of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let the whole race of crea-tures lie A-based be-fore the Lord: What-e'er his might-y hand has formed He gov-erns with a word.

lines: Let the whole race of creatures lie
Whate'er his mighty hand has formed
Ten thousand ages ere the skies
All the long years and worlds to come
Trusting thy wisdom, God of love,
We would not wish to know
What, in the book of thy decrees,
Be this alone our fervent prayer, —
Or joys, or sorrows, may they form
Our souls for heaven and thee.

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
